title: Economy & Finance
description: Talk about personal finance, banking, shopping, budgeting, investments, taxes, and economic systems. Discuss money management, describe financial goals, and understand basic economic concepts. Master the subjunctive for wishes and preferences, the imperfect for past financial situations, and 'saber' vs 'conocer' when talking about financial knowledge.

grammar.title: Presente de Subjuntivo — Wishes, Desires, and Financial Preferences
grammar.content: The present subjunctive expresses wishes, desires, preferences, and doubts about money and financial situations. It is used after expressions like 'querer que', 'esperar que', 'preferir que', 'necesitar que', and 'es importante que'.\\n\\nFormation:\\n- Start with the yo form of the present indicative, drop the -o, add the opposite endings:\\n  - AR verbs: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en\\n  - ER/IR verbs: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an\\n\\nPresent indicative → Present subjunctive:\\n- hablar → hablo → hable, hables, hable, hablemos, habléis, hablen\\n- tener → tengo → tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan\\n- poder → puedo → pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan\\n- querer → quiero → quiera, quieras, quiera, queramos, queráis, quieran\\n- hacer → hago → haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagáis, hagan\\n- saber → sé → sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan\\n- ir → voy → vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayáis, vayan\\n- ser → soy → sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean\\n- venir → vengo → venga, vengas, venga, vengan, vengan\\n\\nFinancial wishes and preferences:\\n- Quiero que mi cuenta tenga más dinero. (I want my account to have more money.)\\n- Espero que los precios bajen pronto. (I hope prices go down soon.)\\n- Prefiero que el banco me ofrezca mejor interés. (I prefer the bank to offer me better interest.)\\n- Necesito que me aprueben el préstamo. (I need them to approve the loan.)
examples: Quiero que ahorremos más dinero este mes. (I want us to save more money this month.)
Espero que mi salario suba el próximo año. (I hope my salary goes up next year.)
Prefiero que la oferta sea válida hoy. (I prefer the deal to be valid today.)
Necesito que me expliquen los impuestos. (I need them to explain the taxes to me.)
Es importante que paguemos a tiempo. (It's important that we pay on time.)

grammar.title: Imperfecto — Past Financial Situations and Habits
grammar.content: The imperfect tense describes past financial situations, habitual spending/saving habits, and ongoing financial states in the past. Use it to talk about what you used to earn, what money was like, or what you regularly did with money.\\n\\nFormation (regular verbs):\\n- AR verbs: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban\\n- ER/IR verbs: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían\\n\\nIrregular verbs in the imperfect (only 3):\\n- ir → iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban\\n- ser → era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran\\n- ver → veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían\\n\\nPast financial habits and situations:\\n- Antes, ganaba menos dinero. (Before, I earned less money.)\\n- Mi padre siempre ahorraba para las emergencias. (My father always saved for emergencies.)\\n- Los precios eran más baratos. (Prices were cheaper.)\\n- Yo tenía una tarjeta de crédito pero nunca la usaba. (I had a credit card but never used it.)\\n\\nImperfect vs Preterite in finance:\\n- Preterite = specific completed action: Gané 2000 euros en enero. (I earned 2,000 euros in January — specific event)\\n- Imperfect = ongoing/habitual: Ganaba 2000 euros al mes. (I used to earn 2,000 euros per month — habitual)
examples: Cuando era estudiante, ahorraba todo el dinero que podía. (When I was a student, I saved all the money I could.)
Mi familia solía ir al supermercado los sábados. (My family used to go to the supermarket on Saturdays.)
Antes, los billetes eran de papel, no digitales. (Before, banknotes were paper, not digital.)
Teníamos una cuenta en el mismo banco desde hace años. (We had an account at the same bank for years.)
Mi madre siempre me decía que no gastara tanto. (My mother always told me not to spend so much.)

grammar.title: Saber vs Conocer — Financial Knowledge
grammar.content: 'Saber' and 'conocer' both translate as 'to know' in English but are used differently in Spanish, especially when talking about financial knowledge.\\n\\nSABER — to know facts, information, or how to do something:\\n- Saber + fact: Sé que los impuestos suben en enero. (I know that taxes go up in January.)\\n- Saber + infinitive = to know how to: Sé invertir en la bolsa. (I know how to invest in the stock market.)\\n- Saber + que = I know that...\\n\\nCONOCER — to be familiar with / to be acquainted with (people, places, things):\\n- Conocer + person/place/thing: Conozco bien los bancos de esta ciudad. (I know the banks in this city well.)\\n- Conocer + un tema = to be familiar with a topic: Conozco la economía española. (I'm familiar with the Spanish economy.)\\n\\nKey difference:\\n- Sé hablar francés. = I know how to speak French. (ability)\\n- Conozco a María. = I know María. (person)\\n- Conozco Madrid. = I'm familiar with Madrid. (place)\\n- Sé la respuesta. = I know the answer. (fact)\\n\\nFinancial knowledge examples:\\n- Sé cómo abrir una cuenta bancaria. (I know how to open a bank account.)\\n- Conozco a mi banquero. (I know my banker.)\\n- No sé nada sobre inversiones. (I don't know anything about investments.)\\n- ¿Conoces alguna buena empresa de ahorro? (Do you know any good savings companies?)
examples: ¿Sabes dónde está el cajero automático más cercano? (Do you know where the nearest ATM is?)
Conozco muy bien las tarifas de este banco. (I'm very familiar with this bank's fees.)
No sé cómo funciona la bolsa, pero quiero aprender. (I don't know how the stock market works, but I want to learn.)
¿Conoces al gerente del banco? (Do you know the bank manager?)
Mi hermano sabe mucho sobre economía y finanzas. (My brother knows a lot about economics and finance.)

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation of Economy & Finance Terms
pronunciation.content: Key pronunciation tips for economy and finance vocabulary:\\n\\n1. Stress on the final syllable (aguda words ending in -n, -s, or vowel):\\n   - el banco (BAHN-koh) — llana, stress on first syllable\\n   - el dinero (dee-NEH-roh) — llana, stress on penult\\n   - la oferta (oh-FEHR-tah) — aguda, stress on final syllable\\n   - el interés (ee-NTEH-rehs) — aguda, stress on final syllable (accent mark)\\n   - el préstamo (PREH-stah-moh) — llana, stress on first syllable\\n\\n2. The 'v' and 'b' sound (they sound the same in Spanish!):\\n   - In Spanish, 'v' and 'b' are pronounced identically — a soft 'b' sound (not English 'v')\\n   - la banca (BAHN-kah) — 'b' is soft, not 'v'\\n   - el banco (BAHN-koh) — same sound\\n   - el valor (bah-LOOR) — 'v' sounds like 'b'\\n\\n3. The rolled 'rr' (trill):\\n   - The double 'rr' always produces a strong trill:\\n   - el dinero (no 'rr')\\n   - la oferta (no 'rr')\\n   - The 'r' at the start of a word also trills:\\n   - el riesgo (reesh-GOH) — 'r' trills\\n   - el mercado (mair-KAH-doh) — no 'rr' or initial 'r'\\n\\n4. The 'j' sound (harsh 'h'):\\n   - el impuesto (im-PUEH-stoh) — 'p' not 'j', but 's' is sharp\\n   - The 'j' appears in: justo (justo), ajustar (to adjust)\\n   - la justicia fiscal (tax justice) — the 'j' is a harsh 'h'\\n\\n5. Silent 'h':\\n   - The 'h' is always silent in Spanish:\\n   - el hipoteca (ee-POH-tee-kah) — 'h' is silent\\n   - el hambre (AHM-breh) — hunger, 'h' silent\\n   - The loanword 'hipoteca' follows the same rule\\n\\n6. The 'c' before 'e' / 'i' (like 'th' in Spain, like 's' in LatAm):\\n   - la cuenta (KWEHN-tah in LatAm, KWEN-tah) — 'c' before 'u' is hard 'k'\\n   - el crédito (KREH-dee-toh) — 'c' before 'e' = 'th' in Spain, 's' in LatAm\\n   - el precio (PREH-see-oh in LatAm) — 'c' before 'e'\\n\\n7. The 'll' sound (like 'y' in most regions):\\n   - la llave (YAH-veh) — key\\n   - The 'll' is pronounced like English 'y' in most of the Spanish-speaking world:\\n   - el sueldo (SOO-el-doh) — no 'll'\\n   - The 'll' does not appear in finance vocabulary as commonly as other sounds.
examples: dinero = dee-NEH-roh (stress on penult — llana)\\n
banco = BAHN-koh (short 'a' sound)\\n
inversión = een-behr-SEE-ohn (stress on antepenult — esdrújula)\\n
impuesto = im-PUEH-stoh (stress on penult — llana)\\n
precio = PREH-see-oh (LatAm) / PREH-thoh-oh (Spain) (stress on first syllable — llana)
hipoteca = ee-POH-tee-kah (silent 'h')\\n
bolsa = BOHL-sah (rolled 'r' not present, soft 's')\\n
sueldo = SOO-el-doh (double vowel sequence)

exercises.question: What does 'la cuenta de ahorros' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La cuenta de ahorros' means savings account. 'Cuenta' = account, 'ahorros' = savings.

exercises.question: Which verb means 'to save (money)' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Ahorrar' means to save money. 'Invertir' = to invest, 'gastar' = to spend, 'ganar' = to earn.

exercises.question: What does 'la inflación' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La inflación' means inflation. 'La deflación' means deflation.

exercises.question: Complete with the present subjunctive: 'Quiero que mi hermana ___ (ahorrar) más dinero.' (I want my sister to save more money.)
exercises.explanation: 'Ahorre' is the present subjunctive of 'ahorrar' for ella/él/usted. We use the subjunctive after 'querer que' to express a wish about someone else's actions.

exercises.question: Complete with the imperfect: 'Antes, yo ___ (ganar) menos dinero.' (Before, I used to earn less money.)
exercises.explanation: 'Ganaba' is the imperfect tense (yo form) of 'ganar'. The imperfect describes past habits and ongoing situations.

exercises.question: What does 'el cajero automático' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'El cajero automático' means ATM (automated teller machine). 'Cajero' = cashier/machine, 'automático' = automatic.

exercises.question: What is the difference between 'saber' and 'conocer' in a financial context?
options: 'Saber' = to know facts/how to; 'conocer' = to be familiar with people/places
'Conocer' is for money; 'saber' is for taxes
exercises.explanation: 'Saber' is used for knowing facts or knowing how to do something (saber + infinitive). 'Conocer' is used for being familiar with people, places, or topics.

exercises.question: Complete with the present subjunctive: 'Es importante que nosotros ___ (pagar) los impuestos a tiempo.' (It's important that we pay taxes on time.)
exercises.explanation: 'Paguemos' is the present subjunctive (nosotros) of 'pagar'. Note the spelling change: 'g' becomes 'gu' to keep the hard 'g' sound before 'e'. The subjunctive is used after 'es importante que'.

exercises.question: What does 'la hipoteca' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La hipoteca' means mortgage. It's the loan used to buy a house or property.

exercises.question: Complete with 'saber' or 'conocer': 'Yo no ___ nada sobre inversiones.' (I don't know anything about investments.)
exercises.explanation: 'Saber' is used when talking about knowing facts or information. 'Saber nada sobre' = to know nothing about. We would use 'conocer' if referring to being familiar with a specific topic or place.

exercises.question: What does 'el IVA' stand for?
exercises.explanation: 'El IVA' stands for 'Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido', which is Spain's equivalent of VAT (Value-Added Tax).

exercises.question: Complete with the imperfect: 'Mi padre siempre ___ (decir) que era mejor ahorrar que gastar.' (My father always used to say it was better to save than to spend.)
exercises.explanation: 'Decía' is the imperfect (él/ella form) of 'decir' (to say). The imperfect describes repeated past actions: 'always used to say'.

exercises.question: Which term means 'supply and demand' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La oferta y la demanda' means supply and demand. 'Oferta' = supply, 'demanda' = demand.

exercises.question: Complete with 'saber' or 'conocer': '___ tú a tu banquero?' (Do you know your banker?)
exercises.explanation: 'Conocer' is used for knowing people. '¿Conoces a tu banquero?' = Do you know your banker (personally)? When the direct object is a person, 'conocer' is required and the personal 'a' is added.

exercises.question: What does 'el desempleo' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'El desempleo' means unemployment. The prefix 'des-' indicates the opposite of 'empleo' (employment).

exercises.question: Complete with the present subjunctive: 'Espero que el banco ___ (dar) más información.' (I hope the bank gives more information.)
exercises.explanation: 'Dé' is the present subjunctive (él/ella/usted) of 'dar'. Note the accent mark on 'dé' to distinguish it from the preposition 'de' (of/from). The subjunctive is used after 'esperar que' to express hope.

exercises.question: What does 'la rebaja' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La rebaja' means discount or sale. During rebajas, stores offer discounted prices. It's a common shopping term in Spanish.

exercises.question: Complete with 'saber' or 'conocer': '___ abrir una cuenta bancaria.' (I know how to open a bank account.)
exercises.explanation: 'Saber' is used with infinitives to express knowing how to do something. 'Sé abrir' = I know how to open. This is an ability, not familiarity with a person or place.

exercises.question: What does 'la economía compartida' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La economía compartida' means the sharing economy (like Uber, Airbnb). 'Compartida' = shared, 'economía' = economy.

exercises.question: Complete with the present subjunctive: 'Mi mamá quiere que yo ___ (invertir) en la bolsa.' (My mom wants me to invest in the stock market.)
exercises.explanation: 'Invierta' is the present subjunctive (yo) of 'invertir'. The stem changes from e→i (invertir → invierta, inviertas, invierta, invirtamos, invirtáis, inviertan). We use subjunctive after 'querer que'.
